questions: Is the tremor present when you are relaxed and not paying attention to it?
Does the tremor change noticeably if you perform a mental task, like counting backwards?
Does the tremor change when you use your right hand for another activity, like drawing a shape with your left hand?
Have you noticed the tremor gets worse when you are stressed or anxious?
Have you ever had a similar symptom in another part of your body?
Did anyone close to you have a similar tremor?
Have you ever been told you have Parkinson's disease or essential tremor?
Does the tremor ever completely stop for a moment?
Have you experienced any major life stress or emotional upset before the tremor began?

results: 1. Formal bedside neurological examination of the right arm and full neurological screening
cranial nerve examination: normal
mental status / cognitive screen: normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): burning pain with pronounced touch sensitivity; vibration and proprioception normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: normal
fundoscopy: normal
tandem gait: normal
walking backward: same pattern as walking forward
running: not attempted
Romberg test, repeated with distraction: negative
muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): normal
cerebellar examination (finger-nose, dysdiadochokinesis, nystagmus): normal
finger-tapping for bradykinesia and decrement: no decrement - argues against Parkinson disease
MRC power in all four limbs: 5/5 throughout
sensory examination (including midline splitting, allodynia): burning pain with pronounced sensitivity to touch, fulfilling allodynia criteria
cognitive screen: normal
2. Entrainment test (ask the patient to tap a rhythm with the left hand)
entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm): POSITIVE - amplitude falls and the rhythm becomes irregular under repetitive voluntary movement of the other side
3. Brain MRI with and without contrast
MRI brain with gadolinium: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional tremor due to functional neurological disorder (FND)

Alternative 1: Malingering (deliberate feigning for external incentive)
Alternative 2: Wilson disease (autosomal recessive copper metabolism disorder)
Alternative 3: The allodynia represents a comorbid functional pain syndrome as part of the same disorder
